info.text: Unit 27 revision bank — production-meeting negotiation, future forms, and the production-planning vocabulary field.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What is the main blocker on aircraft YL-BBX at the start of the meeting?

generalfeedback.text: The shift lead reports that the wiring is complete but the BITE test failed, so the avionics modification cannot be signed off. That failed test is the blocker.

answer.text: The BITE test on the avionics mod failed.

feedback.text: Correct — the wiring is done, but the failed BITE test holds the whole task.

answer.text: The rigging cable set was delivered late.

feedback.text: No — the spares, including the cable set, are already in the store.

answer.text: The cabin task card was signed off early.

feedback.text: No — the cabin activity in Bay 3 simply has a buffer; it is not the blocker.

answer.text: Two mechanics were moved to the wrong bay.

feedback.text: No — the mechanics are reassigned on purpose, from Bay 3 to the mod.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The planner agrees to move two mechanics from Bay 3 onto the avionics modification.

generalfeedback.text: The planner says: “I am going to reassign two mechanics from Bay 3 onto the avionics modification.” So the statement is true.

feedback.text: Correct — the cabin activity has a buffer, so its people can move.
Listen again — the planner clearly agrees to reassign two people from Bay 3.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many hours behind schedule is the aircraft at the start of the meeting? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: “Currently, we are approximately two hours behind.” The answer is 2.

feedback.text: Correct — two hours of slippage.
No — the team is already behind, not on time.

name.text: U27 L4 — deadline for the test

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. By what time must the BITE test be completed? Write it as a 24-hour time with no colon (for example, 1800).

generalfeedback.text: “With two extra mechanics, we will complete the test by 18:00.” The answer is 1800.

feedback.text: Correct — the test is due by 18:00.
No — 22:00 is the release slot, not the test deadline.

name.text: U27 L5 — why rigging keeps priority

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Why does the flight-control rigging keep top priority?

generalfeedback.text: The avionics lead says the rigging “retains absolute priority” because “rushing a control cable is never acceptable.” Safety governs the order of work.

answer.text: Rushing a control cable is never safe.

feedback.text: Correct — safety on the control run is why it stays first.

answer.text: It has by far the shortest lead time here.

feedback.text: No — the cable set has a long lead time of four hours.

answer.text: It needs the fewest people of any job.

feedback.text: No — the reason given is safety, not the number of people.

answer.text: It can run at the same time as ducts.

feedback.text: No — running tasks together is a separate proposal, not the reason.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. How many hours does the cable set take to rig and tension? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: “The cable set requires four hours to rig and tension.” The answer is 4.

feedback.text: Correct — a four-hour lead time on the rigging.
No — two hours is the slippage, not the rigging time.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The spares runner is kept on the job because the spares are still in transit.

generalfeedback.text: “The spares are already available in the store, so the runner is unnecessary.” The runner is removed, so the statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — the spares are in the store, so the runner joins the duct activity.
Listen again — the spares are already in the store, so no runner is needed.

name.text: U27 L8 — start time of the rigging

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. At what time do they start the rigging? Write it as a 24-hour time with no colon (for example, 1815).

generalfeedback.text: “We are commencing the rigging at 18:15, immediately after the test passes.” The answer is 1815.

feedback.text: Correct — the rigging starts at 18:15.
Close — 18:00 is the test deadline; the rigging starts at 18:15.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order, then answer.

WORK ORDER 4471 — YL-BBX
Task: replace the No.2 main-wheel tyre.
Zone: Bay 2.  Estimated man-hours: 1.5.
Spares: tyre and O-ring drawn from store.
Sign-off: one B1 mechanic and one inspector.

Who must sign off the completed task?

generalfeedback.text: The sign-off line names one B1 mechanic and one inspector. Read the sign-off line, not the zone or the spares line.

feedback.text: Correct — the sign-off line asks for both.

answer.text: The production planner on their own.

feedback.text: No — the planner is not named on the sign-off line.
No — a tyre change is a mechanical task, not an avionics one.

answer.text: The store keeper and a planner.

feedback.text: No — the store only issues the spares; it does not sign the task off.

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin note, then decide.

SB 34-1180 (avionics): inspect the ADIRU wiring loom for chafing.
Compliance: within 600 flight hours.  Category: recommended, not mandatory.

Statement: This Service Bulletin is mandatory and must be embodied today.

generalfeedback.text: The category is “recommended, not mandatory,” and compliance is allowed within 600 flight hours — not today. The statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — it is recommended, and there are 600 flight hours to comply.
No — a recommended SB is not mandatory, and the window is 600 flight hours.

questiontext.text:
Read this tech-log entry, then answer.

TECH LOG / MEL — YL-BBX
Defect: forward galley oven inoperative.
MEL ref: 25-30-01, Category C (rectify within 10 days).
Action: item deferred; placard fitted; parts on order.

Under this MEL category, by when must the oven be repaired?

generalfeedback.text: Category C allows rectification within 10 days, so the deferral is legal and the aircraft can fly with the oven placarded.

feedback.text: Correct — Category C gives a 10-day window.
No — the item is deferred and placarded, so the aircraft may fly.
No — the note states ten days, not three.

answer.text: Only at the annual base check.

feedback.text: No — the window is ten days, far sooner than the base check.

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout, then decide.

BITE READOUT — TCAS computer
Result: PASS.  No faults stored.  Self-test complete.

Statement: The readout shows a stored fault that blocks release to service.

generalfeedback.text: The result is PASS with no faults stored, so nothing blocks the release. The statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — a PASS with no stored faults is a clean readout.
No — the readout passed with no faults stored.

questiontext.text:
Read this Airworthiness Directive note, then answer.

AD 2024-07-02: repetitive inspection of the elevator hinge bolts.
Interval: every 200 flight hours.  Status: mandatory (airworthiness).

How often must the elevator hinge bolts be inspected?

generalfeedback.text: The AD sets a repetitive interval of every 200 flight hours, and it is mandatory. Read the interval line.

feedback.text: Correct — a repetitive 200-flight-hour interval.

answer.text: Once at the next base check.

feedback.text: No — it is repetitive, not a one-off task.
No — the trigger is flight hours, not a hard landing.
No — the interval is 200 flight hours, not 600.

name.text: U27 U1 — future form: a promise

questiontext.text:
Complete the promise. Use the word in brackets in the correct future form.

“With two mechanics, we ______ (finish) the test by 18:00.”

Write the two-word verb phrase.

generalfeedback.text: A promise made at the moment of speaking takes will + base verb: will finish.

feedback.text: Correct — will + base verb for a promise.
Correct — the contracted form of will finish.
Use will + the base verb: will finish. Do not add "to".

name.text: U27 U2 — future form: a decided plan

questiontext.text:
Complete the sentence. The plan was decided before the meeting.

“I ______ (reassign) two mechanics from Bay 3.”

Write the verb phrase.

generalfeedback.text: A plan decided beforehand takes be going to: am going to reassign.

feedback.text: Correct — be going to for a decided plan.
Correct — the contracted form.
A pre-decided plan uses be going to: am going to reassign.

name.text: U27 U3 — future form: a fixed arrangement

questiontext.text:
Complete the sentence. The time is already fixed with the team.

“We ______ (start) the rigging at 18:15.”

Write the two-word verb phrase.

generalfeedback.text: A fixed arrangement with a clock time takes the present continuous: are starting.

feedback.text: Correct — present continuous for a fixed arrangement.
Correct — the contracted form.
A fixed time uses the present continuous: are starting.

name.text: U27 U4 — future form: a timetable

questiontext.text:
Complete the sentence. The slot is a fixed schedule you do not control.

“The slot ______ (be) at 22:00.”

Write one word.

generalfeedback.text: A timetable you do not control takes the present simple: is.

feedback.text: Correct — present simple for a fixed timetable.
A timetable uses the present simple: is.

questiontext.text:
Correct the error. Rewrite the underlined verb phrase.

“You have my word. We will to protect the slot.”

Write the two-word verb phrase.

generalfeedback.text: Never put to after will. Use will + base verb: will protect.

feedback.text: Correct — will + base verb, with no "to".
Correct — the contracted form.
Drop the "to": will protect.

name.text: U27 U6 — bank term: the slow step

questiontext.text:
Write the one bank word that fits.

The single slow step that holds up the whole job is the ______.

generalfeedback.text: The slow step that restricts everything is the bottleneck.

feedback.text: Correct — the bottleneck restricts the whole operation.
The slow, limiting step is the bottleneck.

name.text: U27 U7 — bank term: spare time

questiontext.text:
Write the one bank word that fits.

Spare time deliberately built into the plan for problems is a ______.

generalfeedback.text: Reserve time built into a plan is a buffer.

feedback.text: Correct — a buffer absorbs problems.
Reserve time in a plan is a buffer.

name.text: U27 U8 — bank term: the driving chain

questiontext.text:
Write the two-word bank term that fits.

The chain of tasks that sets the earliest possible finish is the ______.

generalfeedback.text: The chain that sets the earliest finish is the critical path.

feedback.text: Correct — the critical path drives the turnaround.
The driving chain of tasks is the critical path.

questiontext.text: Match each production-planning term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: slot = the fixed ready time; manpower = the workers you have; slippage = time fallen behind; milestone = a key checkpoint; handover = the pass to the next team.

correctfeedback.text: All matched — the vocabulary field is secure.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are wrong — check the meanings again.

incorrectfeedback.text: Re-read the vocabulary bank and try the pairs once more.

answer.text: the fixed time the aircraft must be ready
the number of workers you have for the job
the time a task has fallen behind the plan
a key checkpoint that shows progress
the pass of a job to the next team

name.text: U27 V2 — term and word partner

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb or phrase it usually goes with (its word partner).

generalfeedback.text: protect the slot; clear a blocker; raise a work order; sign off the task card; hit a milestone.

correctfeedback.text: All matched — you know the collocations.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some partners are wrong — look at the vocabulary bank's word-partner column.

incorrectfeedback.text: Check the word-partner column and try again.

questiontext.text: Which verb goes best with slot in a production meeting?

generalfeedback.text: We protect the slot — we work to keep the fixed release time. The other verbs do not partner with slot.

feedback.text: Correct — protect the slot is the standard collocation.
No — you tension a cable, not a slot.
No — you embody a Service Bulletin, not a slot.
No — you placard a deferred defect, not a slot.

questiontext.text: An aircraft that cannot fly until a fault is fixed is described by which term?

generalfeedback.text: AOG means “aircraft on ground”: it cannot fly until the defect is rectified. The other terms name documents or time, not a grounded aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct — aircraft on ground.
No — lead time is a waiting period, not a grounded aircraft.
No — a work order is the document that authorises a job.
No — the turnaround is the whole arrival-to-release period.
